description: A transitional-style kitchen photographed at standing eye-level, roughly five feet off the floor, using a normal lens and a three-quarter corner composition that angles across the kitchen island and draws the eye toward the cooking wall. The ceiling is clad in white-painted shiplap planks running horizontally, punctuated by two warm brass canopy mounts at center. The upper cabinetry is all painted creamy white with inset frames and a pair of glass-front uppers flanking a large applied-moulding range hood in the same white finish. Backsplash tiles are honed marble in a classic brick pattern, soft grey-white with subtle veining running from counter height to the underside of the upper cabinets. A professional-style range with multiple brass knob accents sits center-right against the wall, with a brass gooseneck bridge faucet at the island sink. The kitchen island features a painted warm-oak base with vertical shaker panel detailing and a thick bright-white quartz countertop. Three round-top adjustable-height stools with dark patinated iron bases and worn walnut seats are tucked under the island overhang. On the island surface: a clear glass vase holding a fresh stem of dark-green foliage, a small wooden cutting board, and a loose arrangement of fresh vegetables including broccoli and tomatoes. Light enters from a pair of double-panel wood-framed French doors at the left, flooding the left wall and island surface with soft natural daylight. The overall palette is creamy white, warm light oak, bright white quartz, with antique brass hardware accents throughout. The flooring visible at the bottom of the frame is wide-plank light oak.
